course.learn: Change management is the controlled process for planning, approving, testing, implementing, documenting, and—if necessary—reversing technical changes.
course.why: Uncontrolled changes can create outages and security gaps. A repeatable process reduces surprise and preserves accountability.
course.example: Before updating a production firewall, the team documents the change, assesses impact, gets approval, tests it, schedules a maintenance window, and prepares a rollback plan.
course.exam: Common exam clues: approval, impact analysis, maintenance window, test results, backout plan, ownership, stakeholders, SOP, and documentation.
